items.title: Call to Order
notes: Mayor Watters welcomed everyone and called the meeting to order.

items.title: Land Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor MacDonald read the land acknowledgement.

items.title: Addendums and Corrections to the Agenda
notes: None.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest Under the Municipal Conflict of Interest
notes: Act

Councillor Jefferson declared a conflict of interest related to discussions pertaining to the Fergus Business Improvement Area or the parking strategy due to her ownership of a building and a business within the BIA catchment area.

items.title: CAO Executive Summary
notes: D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer highlighted the strategic plan, outlining the goals and objectives and the linkages between the Strategic Plan, the Business Plan and the Draft Budget. He noted the property taxation impact by area and the overall Township Property Taxation Impact resulting in a 3.49% increase in taxation. D. Wilson indicated currently the Budget includes the following:
 Maintaining existing service levels
 Asset Management investment
 Much needed staff positions
 Termite Management Program Implementation
 Reduced provincial grant funding
 $200,000 TIEG payment

items.title: Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer
notes: provided an over and summary, including asset management, general budget information and the public engagement process undertaken.

Mark Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer provided an overview of the tax supported operating budget, including operating budget facts and how the budget works, funding challenges, significant formatting changes, contributions to capital and major impact areas.
A. McNabb reviewed the Debt Analysis, debt payments by service type and projected debt as a percentage of revenue.
Staff responded to questions regarding potential impacts of the municipality taking on debt to fund the new Operations Centre, and the process if the debt payments could not be made.

items.title: New Township Operations Centre Update - Grant Funding Opportunities
notes: and Class C Construction Cost Estimate
Report from B. Buehler, Operations Centre Project Manager Brandon Buehler, Operations Centre Project Manager provided an overview of the report, indicating the purpose of the report is to:
 provide a further update on grant funding opportunities for the new Township Operations Centre;
 Seek Council approval to submit an application for grant funding from the FCM – Municipal Fleet Electrification Grant Funds for the project; and,

 present the “Class C” construction cost estimate for the project He explained the Project Team has investigated grant funding opportunities from the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM), the new Sustainable Municipal and Community Buildings Fund and the Municipal Fleet Electrification Grant Fund. He further explained the eligibility requirements and indicated this project would not meet the criteria for the Sustainable Municipal and Community Buildings Fund.

B. Buehler provided additional details on the Municipal Fleet Electrification Grant Fund and indicated the project team will continue to explore this avenue as well as other funding and third-party partnerships that support complementary aspects of the project.

Staff responded to questions regarding collaboration with the Climate Change Coordinator, investigation of hybrid heating/cooling opportunities, options for solar initiatives and solar storage and submission timelines.

items.title: Fleet Policy
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer
Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the report.

items.title: 2025 Fees and Charges By-Law
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer
Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the report and staff responded to questions.
Mayor Watters called for a 10 minute recess, the meeting resumed at 10:40 am.

items.title: Staffing Strategy
notes: Rashid Hasan, Chief Human Resources Officer provided an overview of the
staffing strategy, including the guiding principles, the compensation philosophy, the justification process, and the learning and development program.
Dan Wilson, CAO indicated there is no increase in taxation to support staffing. He outlined the staffing strategy funding formula, the 2025 proposed new staffing and the proposed funding strategy.

Staff responded to questions regarding the justification required to put forward a staffing request, historical hiring practices, the use of comparator municipalities, positions rated based on need, the new box office position at the Fergus Grand Theatre, the coop/assistant positions, the flexibility of the shared position, timing of the By-law Clerk and Licensing Officer, and minor restructuring to find efficiencies.
Mayor Watters called a recess for lunch, the meeting resumed at 1:00pm.

items.title: Delegations @ 1:00pm
notes: Councillor Jefferson, having declared a conflict of interest, left the meeting.

items.title: Fergus Business Improvement Area re Budget
notes: Fred Gordon, BIA Administrator expressed his gratitude on behalf of the Fergus BIA for all the hard work of Councillors and staff. He outlined the members of the incoming executive and highlighted various exciting and successful events, including the Classic Car Show, Tartan Day, the Medieval Fair and many others. He outlined some of the challenges this past year with the construction and noted several new initiatives planned for 2025.
F. Gordon indicated to continue to expand events, programs and beautification projects, there will be a 7.68% increase to the levy.

items.title: Elora Business Improvement Area re Budget
notes: MacLean Hann, Elora BIA Chair echoed the comments of Fred Gordon and expressed his gratitude on behalf of the Elora BIA for all the hard work of Councillors and staff, making all efforts very worthwhile. He provided an overview of the food events, including, Eloralisious, Elora Burger battle, and Food Day Canada. He highlighted other events and activities such as Starlight Shopping, and the lighting up of Elora to brighten the streets.
M. Hann noted the burden of the garbage costs and missed pick ups and he looks forward to finding a solution to the garbage problems in the downtown areas.

items.title: Tax Supported Operating Budget
notes: Mark Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer provided an overview of the 2025 tax supported operating budget summary. He reviewed the average residential tax bill breakdown and noted the significant areas impacting the tax supported operating budget.

Staff from the various departments responded to question regarding the increase in fees related to the annual fire and rescue dispatch fees from the City of Guelph, the tile drain loan process, the status of the new and improvements planning for the street lights in Fergus, use of the concession area at the Jefferson Elora Community Centre, the new customer service clerk position, and new initiatives to support physician recruitment.
Mayor Watters called for a 5 minute recess, the meeting resumed at 2:38 pm

items.title: Tax Supported 3-Year Operating Budget
notes: Mark Bradey continued to provide an overview of the tax supported 3- year operating budget and the water/wastewater operating budget.

items.title: 2025 Capital Budget
notes: Mark Bradey provided background and an overview of the 2025 draft capital budget.

Staff responded to questions regarding the software required to manage and monitor short term rental licensing, DEI initiatives for the upcoming year, funding for cyber security, the Belwood Hall renovations and budget, and future renovations to the Jefferson Elora Community Centre.

items.title: 10-Year Capital Budget
notes: Mark Bradey provided background and an overview of the 10-Year Capital Budget and responded to questions regarding an update on the status of the Jefferson Elora Community Centre parking lot project, funding available for the Bissell Park Multi-Use Pad project, and a reduction in funding for future strategic plans due to internal process.

items.title: 2025 Draft Business Plan
notes: Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer

Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer indicated the 2025 Business Plan outlines the recommended staff initiatives to focus on throughout the year. He outlined several other initiatives not necessarily captured in the budget, such as exploration of a garbage solution or paid parking, design of Confederation Park, second annual golf tournament, community planning permit system, etc.

D. Wilson responded to questions regarding fire department community engagement, provision of more parking and wayfinding signage, employee learning and development program, development of a climate change action plan, a permanent shuttle bus program, and the need for improved accessible parking.
Councillor Wilton suggested a broadening of the language to include affordable housing in the action item related to the strategic initiative:
Ensure people working in our community can afford to live here.
Brett Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development agreed to add “including affordable housing” to the end of the sentence.
Members of Council discussed an adjournment versus continuing with the meeting.

items.title: Ontario Regulation 284/09 - 2025 Budget
notes: Report from M. Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer Mark Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer provided an overview of the report indicating this is a routine matter required to be passed annually.

items.title: 2025 Draft Budget
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer
Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer summarized the budget deliberations.

items.title: Adjourn
notes: Mayor Municipal Clerk

motions.item_title: New Township Operations Centre Update - Grant Funding Opportunities
motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington endorses and directs staff to submit an application for grant funding from the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) – Municipal Fleet Electrification Fund; AND THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington receives for information the updated “Class C” construction cost estimate for construction of the new Township Operations Centre.

motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington authorize the Mayor and Clerk to sign a By-Law to endorse a new Fleet Policy for the Township of Centre Wellington. AND THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington direct staff to enact and adhere to the Fleet Policy effective December 31, 2024.
